requirement: Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Each group and each input MUST be a collapsible disclosure element, with groups expanded and inputs collapsed by default, so readers can move between groups and open individual sources. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. An outline input MUST show its file, selector, kind, and current inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each outline input subsection MUST show the node's current source text in a fenced code block and say when its hash no longer matches; a requirements or definition input subsection MUST show its recorded text. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
rationale:
**Verdict: gaps remain. Most of the requirement is implemented and tested, but the badge and group-order obligations are not marked, and two obligations have no test assertions.** **What is implemented and tested** - `render_detail_sections` in `src/index.rs` produces the page structure. - It renders the badge, a block-quoted body under a "Requirement" or "Example" heading, a Rationale section, FIXME references, and the Inputs groups. - Groups render as `
` and inputs as collapsed `
`. - `DefinitionEdges::current` and `group` build edges from current `{impl}` and `{test}` references and from anchors. They also pick up `{cite}` edges from the definition's own text. - Sorting into Implementation, Tests, Referenced definitions and Other sources is done here. - `render_input`, `render_source_location`, `push_code_block` and `code_language` render the following. - Outline inputs show file, selector, kind and line range. - A stale-hash warning is shown when the hash no longer matches. - Requirements and definition inputs show their recorded text. - Code fences carry `rust,noplayground`, `markdown`, `json`, `ini` (for TOML), `java`, `javascript`, `typescript` and `python`. - Tests cover much of this: - `detail_page_renders_markdown_and_highlighted_input_sections` covers the badge URL, the quote, the rationale, the outline details, the hash warning and the fences. - `detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures` covers group order, the anchor-based grouping, and the open/collapsed disclosure counts. - `common_input_extensions_select_highlighting_languages` covers the language mapping. - `index_lists_examples_and_links_their_detail_pages` covers the "Example" label. - `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` covers the FIXME strings. **Gaps** 1. **Unmarked implementation of the badge image and alt text.** - `shield_badge` in `src/lib.rs:433` builds the Shields.io `` and its `alt` text. The requirement specifies both. - It carries only `{impl}` for `requirements.references.book_badges` and `safe_badges`, not for `detail_format`. - The state label and colour functions (`EvidenceState::label` and `color`) are marked only for `requirements.index.state`. - Under the targets rule, a source that produces an output the definition specifies is an implementer. This part of the requirement therefore lacks an `{impl}` reference. 2. **Unmarked group order.** `InputGroup::ALL` (`src/index.rs:526`), the constant that fixes the required group order, sits in an `impl` block that has no `{impl}` marker for `detail_format`. Only `heading` and `id` are marked. 3. **No test of the alt text on a detail page.** The tests assert only the badge URL (`img.shields.io/badge/evidence-Valid-237346`). The only `alt=` assertions are for requirement-reference badges and `shield_badge` unit cases, not the detail page's state badge. 4. **No test of requirements-input details.** - Nothing checks that a requirements input shows each matched definition's full name, file and inclusive line range. - The grouped test checks only the `requirements selection rules.base` label. - Nothing checks that recorded text for requirements or definition inputs is rendered with Markdown highlighting. 5. **Other test gaps.** Test-kind anchors and cited definitions' own grouping are not tested separately. There is no test of the "Unreadable evidence record" path. None of these gaps carries a FIXME comment, so the judgment is false rather than FIXME.

text: :::{req} detail_format

Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Each group and each input MUST be a collapsible disclosure element, with groups expanded and inputs collapsed by default, so readers can move between groups and open individual sources. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. An outline input MUST show its file, selector, kind, and current inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each outline input subsection MUST show the node's current source text in a fenced code block and say when its hash no longer matches; a requirements or definition input subsection MUST show its recorded text. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references.

:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
